subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: What should OpenClaw do when a provider emits a bare no-argument tool marker such as `[tool: exec]` instead of a structured tool call?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but a bare marker lacks executable arguments, so safely fixing it requires maintainer intent on retry, fallback, warning, or provider/model mitigation rather than a mechanical parser change.

options.title: Retry or fail over with diagnostics
options.body: Treat the bare marker as an invalid degraded tool intent, retry or fall back through a defined provider/runtime path, and surface a clear diagnostic when no safe recovery exists.

options.title: Warn and block execution
options.body: Strip the marker from user-visible text, do not execute anything, and return a clear warning that the model emitted an unusable tool call.

options.title: Provider-specific mitigation
options.body: Add targeted prompt, schema, or capability-shaping mitigation for affected MiniMax/DeepSeek-style routes after live provider proof identifies a stable trigger.

recommendation.title: Retry or fail over with diagnostics
recommendation.body: Treat the bare marker as an invalid degraded tool intent, retry or fall back through a defined provider/runtime path, and surface a clear diagnostic when no safe recovery exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history points to Vincent Koc as the recent owner of the runtime snapshot and release behavior around the repair and sanitizer paths.
